items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: when we were recording the lovely Al Jarreau stuff

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and boy, I’m very happy to have Chuck Findley with me today. And one of your colleagues, who is a decent trumpet player named Jerry Hey said, “Chuck Findley can play anything.”

Well that’s a lovely compliment I must say, Monk. Well I’ll tell you that really goes back to like when we were recording the lovely Al Jarreau stuff and just a lot of ridiculous things. And Jerry was a wonderful trumpet player when he could play, but then he had an issue with his throat and he couldn’t play anymore so he just became a writer, which he was anyhow, and he became a fantastic commercial writer. But Jerry would always, he would play everything he wrote before he brought it to a session, and, to make…

That is so interesting because I went and revisited that and it’s literally four bars plus a two-beat pick-up. And the fact that it brought you that recognition and that — Herb Alpert had something to do with that song, didn’t he?
